title: Ideal Gas Equation
notes: **Ideal gas:** a theoretical gas whose molecules have negligible volume and no intermolecular forces.

**Combining laws:** Boyle's law ($PV = \text{const}$ at constant $T$), Charles's law ($V/T = \text{const}$ at constant $P$), and Avogadro's law ($V/n = \text{const}$ at constant $P,T$) combine into $PV = nRT$.
**Universal gas constant:** $R = 8.314\,\text{J/mol}\cdot\text{K}$. It is the same for all ideal gases.
**Alternative forms:** $PV = Nk_BT$, where $N$ is the number of molecules and $k_B = R/N_A = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\,\text{J/K}$ is the Boltzmann constant.
**Real gases:** deviate from ideal behaviour at high pressure and low temperature, where molecular volume and intermolecular forces become significant.
